text:
maya_support: Hi @leila_csm — Horizon just opened an escalation: they're seeing intermittent 429s and large latency spikes during their Q2 marketing send. Customer notes baseline ~130 QPS, brief peaks up to ~1.4k QPS for 10–20m windows. Can we triage?

leila_csm: forwarding logs from Horizon ops — they reported ~18% request failures (429) during the peak window yesterday 10:14–10:35 UTC. Pool is horizon-dedicated-1, min=2, max=8, autoscale target_util=0.65.

jason_oncall: I'm looking at metrics now. Initial graphs show per-GPU utilization jumping to ~95% and a lot of request queueing. Autoscaler did add nodes but only after ~6m because of cooldown + scale_step limits. That delay correlates with the 429 spike.

tom_infra: autoscaler config for that pool: 
```
target_utilization: 0.65
cooldown_seconds: 300
scale_step: 1
min_nodes: 2
max_nodes: 8
```
That's pretty conservative for short 10–20m spikes.

jason_oncall: Also seeing a noisy-tenant signal — one long-lived batch job from Horizon's analytics client is chewing KV cache and memory, reducing concurrency. Log snippet: "kv_cache: evict_rate high for tenant:horizon_batch_72". That amplifies the saturation.

maya_support: Customer also asked why their bill spiked — lots of retries + surge capacity. They want a short-term mitigation for the next campaign in ~48h and a long-term sizing plan.

leila_csm: Proposed immediate mitigations?

tom_infra: Short-term actions we can apply immediately (with approval):
- Increase min_nodes to 5 for the campaign window
- Reduce cooldown_seconds to 60s so autoscaler reacts faster
- Increase scale_step to 2 to let it add capacity faster
- Temporarily enable burst_capacity to let the pool borrow small shared capacity

jason_oncall: Long-term recommendations:
- Lower target_utilization for this tenant to ~0.6 given burstiness
- Reserve headroom: keep ~30% free capacity for known campaign windows
- Implement per-tenant session limits / soft quotas to prevent single batch jobs from starving others
- Tune KV cache TTLs for batch workflows (default 30m -> 5m for analytics jobs)

maya_support: Repro steps I used locally to reproduce 429s:
1) run a very simple fanout loop:
```
for i in `seq 1 1400`; do curl -s -H "X-Customer: horizon" https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate & done
```
2) watch for 429s after ~30s when the pool saturates. (This is noisy but reproduces the immediate saturation pattern.)

jason_oncall: Added a more realistic ramp test suggestion (k6):
```
k6 run --vus 400 --duration 30m --rps 1400 script.js
```
script.js should include the X-Customer header and realistic prompt sizes. Use this to validate config changes pre-campaign.

leila_csm: Cost note: increasing min_nodes 2->5 for 2 hours nightly during the campaign is estimated ~ $1,200. Horizon said they'd accept that if it prevents errors.

maya_support: Timeline for applying changes?

tom_infra: I can roll min_nodes & cooldown changes now if ops approve. ETA: 15m to stage config, ~5m propagate. Will coordinate a short maintenance window or do immediate change if CSM approves.

autoscale-bot: change_request accepted by infra: pool=horizon-dedicated-1 min_nodes=5 cooldown_seconds=60 scale_step=2 — requested by tom_infra at 1948765450.

jason_oncall: Follow-up plan: schedule a post-campaign deep-dive. We'll collect traces, quantify noisy-tenant impact, and propose a permanent sizing model (headroom, min_nodes schedule, cache tuning). Dropping runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-surge-response

leila_csm: Please ping Horizon ops to confirm acceptance and agree a pre-warm test 1h before their next campaign send. Also capture a short watch rotation for the first 30m of the window.

maya_support: Thanks team — I'll update the customer and close after the campaign verification.
